nativeWasmParity.method: throwaway Node host instantiating the built bytes and calling engine_alloc/engine_call/engine_reply_ptr/engine_reply_len; native reply from the same dispatch_json entry point (examples/candidate_command). Request bytes identical per case (hashed).
nativeWasmParity.invokedBuffer: the instantiated bytes are the artifact above (hash recorded per case in final/wasm-*.meta.json)
nativeWasmParity.interpretation: Every error reply and every non-numeric report value (schema ids, identities, statuses, flags, counts, strings) is byte-identical between native and the built wasm32 artifact. Success replies differ only in platform libm last bits; the maximum relative difference is 3.26e-11 (on a near-zero aero moment of 3.6e-7 N m), inside the standing 1e-9 native/WASM precision. This is pre-existing: the untouched legacy command differs between native and wasm on the same host (burnoutAltitude 107.8003368374231 vs 107.80033683742307, plus three near-zero telemetry values). No float-rounding policy was introduced.

residuals.detail: six_dof.rs record_telemetry collects one display point per macro step before rail exit and after apogee (and every fifth step otherwise) with no internal cap; bounded only by MAX_MACRO_ITERATIONS=5e6 and then decimated to MAX_TELEMETRY_POINTS for the wire in models.rs. The candidate path sets record_telemetry=false, so simulate_candidate cannot reach it.

residuals.detail: this serde_json build has no float_roundtrip feature, so re-parsing a 17-digit decimal can move a value by one ULP; whole-report text round trips are therefore not an equality proof
